_comment: Seed classification lists. 'seed' entries come from the brief and from
senders observed live on the business account. Anything the tool derives
from 90-day data is written into config/filters.<account>.json tagged
with source='derived', so you can always tell what you specified from
Matching is on the sending domain, including subdomain. Gmail's from:
operator matches the domain and its subdomains, so listing 'substack.com'

personal._promotional_comment: Skip-inbox is only safe for domains that send NOTHING but marketing. Deliberately excluded: uber.com (ride receipts), sevenrooms.com (reservation confirmations), livenation.com (event tickets). All three mix marketing with mail you would be sorry to archive; Gmail's own Promotions category catches their marketing anyway.

business._platform_comment: Machine-only senders: deploy notices, renewal reminders, usage alerts. Nothing here is ever triggered by a human, so it can leave the inbox. google.com is deliberately absent -- Calendar invitations, Docs comments and Drive shares all come from google.com, and a blanket skip-inbox rule there would hide meeting invites. Filter Workspace admin mail on its full sender address instead.
business._collab_comment: Platforms whose mail is generated BY A PERSON doing something -- commenting on a PR, mentioning you, assigning a task. These get the Admin label so they are findable, but they stay in the inbox, per the rule that mail with a person behind it is never archived automatically.

_never_auto_classify_comment: Domains that must never be bucketed automatically, because mail from them is usually a person even though the domain looks generic.
